title: Sunny and the Butterfly
description: Little Sonny the quokka follows a beautiful butterfly through a sun-dappled clearing. A light, dreamy bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny was sitting in the clearing when he saw it — a butterfly, orange and black, drifting on the soft afternoon air.

It moved without hurrying. Without any particular plan, as far as Sunny could tell. Just floating, tilting, rising on invisible currents, settling briefly on a flower petal, then lifting off again.

Sunny got up and followed it. Gently. Slowly. Careful not to startle it.

The butterfly seemed unconcerned with Sunny entirely. It drifted ahead, leading him through the dappled light under the tall gum trees, over a low rock, along the edge of the little creek.

Sunny followed, stepping carefully, watching the wings open and close and open again.

He had nowhere else to be. This was enough.

Eventually the butterfly rose high, caught an upward breeze, and drifted away above the treetops until Sunny couldn't see it anymore.

He stood where he was for a moment, looking up at the blue sky.

Then he smiled, turned around, and walked slowly back through the dappled light. He felt lighter, somehow, than when he started.

The creek murmured beside him. A bird called, once, from somewhere above.

Sunny found a soft patch of ground near a flowering hakea and lay down, looking up through the leaves at the sky.

He wondered where the butterfly went. He hoped it was somewhere beautiful.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, orange butterfly. Goodnight, light and drifting afternoon.
